text:
As the Leduc Center for Civic Engagement marks an important 
transition, we celebrate and honor the remarkable career of 
Deirdre Healy, whose retirement closes a chapter defined by deep 
commitment, thoughtful leadership, and lasting impact. 
For years, Deirdre has been a cornerstone of the Leduc Center, helping 
to shape its mission and bring its values to life through meaningful 
partnerships, student engagement, and community-centered work. 
Her dedication to civic engagement was never abstract—it was 
personal, intentional, and rooted in a genuine belief in the power of 
students and communities working together for the public good. 
Deirdre played a vital role in supporting students as they navigated 
service-learning experiences, internships, and leadership opportunities 
that connected classroom learning with real-world challenges. She 
understood that civic engagement is not just about participation, but 
about preparation—equipping students with the skills, confidence, 
and sense of responsibility needed to become engaged citizens and 
leaders. Countless students credit Deirdre with helping them find their 
voice, clarify their purpose, and see themselves as agents of change. 
Equally impactful was Deirdre’s work with community partners. 
She built relationships grounded in trust, respect, and mutual 
benefit, ensuring that partnerships were not transactional but truly 
collaborative. Community organizations knew they could rely on 
Deirdre—not only for coordination and support, but for thoughtful 
listening and a shared commitment to meaningful outcomes. Through 
her efforts, the Leduc Center strengthened its role as a bridge between 
the university and the broader community. 
Within the Center, Deirdre was known for her steady presence, 
institutional knowledge, and generosity of spirit. She mentored 
colleagues, supported new initiatives, and approached challenges with 
professionalism and care. Her work often happened behind the scenes, 
but its impact was visible everywhere—in successful programs, strong 
partnerships, and a culture that values service and civic responsibility. 
We extend our deepest gratitude for her years of service to the Leduc 
Center, to UMass Dartmouth, and to the many students and community 
members whose lives she touched. Her legacy will continue through 
the programs she helped build, the relationships she nurtured, and the 
countless individuals inspired by her example. We wish Deirdre all the 
best in this next chapter and thank her for a career that truly embodied 
the spirit of civic engagement. 
HONORING DEIRDRE HEALY'S SERVICE
